title: Best Haier Dehumidifier (2026): 20, 35 & 50-Pint Smart Dry
dek: Haier owns GE Appliances, but its own Smart Dry lineup has a story of its own. Here's which model to buy, and what to check before you do.
description: The best Haier dehumidifier for your space: the 20-, 35- and 50-pint Smart Dry models compared, plus recall history, manuals, filters and the GE connection.
intro: Shopping for a **Haier dehumidifier** is mostly a question of size. The current Smart Dry lineup comes in three capacities — 20, 35 and 50 pints a day — plus a 50-pint version with a built-in pump. All of them are ENERGY STAR certified, all use the same adaptive fan control, and the step up in capacity is as much about how damp the room is as how big it is.

The brand has more name recognition than its dehumidifier shelf space suggests, largely because Haier has owned GE Appliances since 2016. That doesn't mean the two lines are built the same way, and it's worth understanding the relationship, the brand's recall history on older models, and the limited independent reliability data before you buy.
We compared the current models using Haier's published specs, ENERGY STAR listings, CPSC recall records and owner feedback, then sorted them by the job each one does best.
topPicksLead: The **Haier 20-Pint (QDHR20LZ)** is the best Haier for most bedrooms, offices and small rooms, while the 50-pint models take over for basements.

products.name: Haier 20-Pint Smart Dry Dehumidifier (QDHR20LZ)
pros: Smart Dry adjusts fan speed to room conditions
Gravity hose option for continuous draining
cons: One-year warranty covers parts only, not labor
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a bedroom, home office or guest room, 20 pints is the right amount of dehumidifier, and this is the most approachable way into Haier's lineup. It carries the same convenience features as the bigger models without the bigger cabinet.
products.performance: Haier rates it at 20 pints a day for damp spaces up to about 1,000 square feet. Smart Dry automatically adjusts fan speed as the room dries, which keeps it from running harder than it needs to. You can empty the internal tank by hand or attach a hose for gravity draining. Compare it with other compact units in our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Haier 35-Pint Smart Dry Dehumidifier (QDHR35LZ)
pros: Rated to use nearly 15% less energy than non-certified peers
More extraction for the same room size
cons: Same rated coverage as the 20-pint model
products.whyWeLoveIt: Haier rates this model for the same 1,000-square-foot band as the 20-pint, but for "very damp" spaces. That makes it the pick for a musty lower-level room or laundry area that's the same size as a bedroom but far more humid.
products.performance: At 35 pints a day, it pulls more water from the same footprint, so it reaches its setpoint faster and cycles off sooner in a soggy room. Its ENERGY STAR certification means it's rated to use nearly 15% less energy than a similar non-certified unit. With a hose attached, it can run unattended in a basement corner. See how it stacks up across brands in our [best dehumidifier for 1,000 sq ft](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-1000-sq-ft/) roundup.

products.name: Haier 50-Pint Smart Dry Dehumidifier (QDHR50LZ)
pros: Covers up to about 1,500 sq ft of wet space
Digital display and Smart Dry fan control
products.whyWeLoveIt: A full basement or wet utility space needs the top of the portable range, and the 50-pint is the Haier built for it. If there's a floor drain nearby, the standard version with a gravity hose is all you need.
products.performance: Haier rates it at 50 pints a day for wet spaces up to roughly 1,500 square feet, with a 15-pint internal tank or gravity-hose draining. No drain nearby? The **QPHR50LZ** shares the same capacity and adds a built-in pump that lifts water up to 16 feet to a sink or window, with a rated draw of 530 watts and a maximum of 50 dBA. For more basement options, see our [best dehumidifier for basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) guide.
products.notes: Choose the QPHR50LZ if your only drain is a laundry sink or a window above the unit.

blocks.caption: Coverage figures are Haier's own ratings.

blocks.text: We don't run a test lab. We compared Haier's published capacities and coverage ratings with ENERGY STAR certification data, checked every model against CPSC recall notices, and read owner reviews for recurring complaints such as noisy compressors, inaccurate humidity readings and early failures.

Because Haier publishes less independent reliability data than brands like Frigidaire or Midea, we weighted features that reduce risk — ENERGY STAR efficiency, continuous drainage, a pump option — and we're upfront below about where the evidence is thin.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Haier dehumidifier

items.label: Capacity matched to dampness
items.text: The 20- and 35-pint models share a rated room size. Pick the 35 if the room smells musty or has visible condensation, not because it's bigger.

items.label: The right drain setup
items.text: Standard models drain by gravity or bucket. If the nearest drain is above the unit, choose the pump-equipped QPHR50LZ.

items.label: The full model number
items.text: Check the suffix on any listing, especially secondhand. Older Haier models in the HM and HEN series predate the current Smart Dry generation.

items.label: Warranty terms
items.text: Haier's one-year coverage is parts only. If longer protection matters, compare with sibling brand GE in our [Haier vs. GE comparison](/compare/haier-vs-ge-dehumidifier/).

items.label: A separate hygrometer
items.text: Built-in sensors can read several points off. An inexpensive standalone meter confirms the room is really in the 30–50% range.

sections.heading: Who makes Haier dehumidifiers? The GE connection

blocks.text: Haier bought GE Appliances from General Electric in 2016, so GE-badged dehumidifiers now come from a Haier-owned company. You might assume the two lines are the same hardware. Not quite: ENERGY STAR records show GE's current dehumidifiers are built under license by Midea, while the manufacturer behind Haier's own Smart Dry units isn't published in the same way.

The family resemblance is still obvious. Both lines use "Smart Dry" branding, and the pump-equipped 50-pint models line up closely on paper, including a 15-pint bucket, three fan speeds and a 530-watt draw. It's fair to call them close siblings; it would be overreaching to call them identical. Our [best GE dehumidifier](/best/best-ge-dehumidifier/) guide covers that side of the family.

sections.heading: Is Haier reliable? Recalls and the evidence

blocks.text: The most detailed independent bench review of a Haier dehumidifier covered the older 65-pint DE65EM. It scored durability 2 out of 5, pointing to a prior-generation model whose retailer reviews were more than half negative and to owner reports of compressor and filter problems around the two-year mark. It also found humidity control inconsistent and the built-in hygrometer reading 5 to 6 points off — though energy efficiency earned top marks. That model predates today's Smart Dry units, so treat it as context, not a verdict.

In 2021, the CPSC announced a recall of roughly 2 million dehumidifiers sold under 20 brand names, all made by New Widetech, after 107 reported fires and about $17 million in property damage. The affected Haier models were:

items: Only units made before September 1, 2017 and sold between February 2009 and August 2017

blocks.title: Buying used?
blocks.text: None of the current QDHR or QPHR models are covered, but check any secondhand or estate-sale Haier against CPSC.gov before plugging it in. Friedrich models from the same recall carry a trickier twist, explained in our [best Friedrich dehumidifier](/best/best-friedrich-dehumidifier/) guide.

sections.heading: Haier dehumidifier manual, filter and repair basics

blocks.text: Most owner questions about a Haier dehumidifier come down to three things: finding the manual, keeping the filter clean and figuring out why it stopped pulling water.

items: **Manual:** Haier posts owner's manuals and installation instructions on its appliance support site. Search by the full model number printed on the label on the back or side of the unit.

**Filter:** The air filter is a washable mesh screen behind the front or rear grille. When the clean-filter reminder lights up, slide it out, rinse it in warm water, let it dry completely and reset the reminder. Our [replacement filter guide](/guides/dehumidifier-replacement-filter/) covers when a new one makes sense.

**How to use it:** Set a target humidity around 45–50%, choose auto fan or Smart Dry, and attach the hose if you don't want to empty the bucket. Make sure the bucket is seated fully, or the unit won't run.

**Repair and parts:** If it runs but collects no water, check the filter, the room temperature (coils can frost below about 65°F) and the bucket switch before calling for service. Our [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) guide walks through the full checklist.

blocks.text: The **Haier 20-Pint (QDHR20LZ)** is the best Haier dehumidifier for most small rooms, the **35-Pint (QDHR35LZ)** handles damper rooms of the same size, and the **50-Pint (QDHR50LZ)** is the basement pick, with the **QPHR50LZ** adding a pump when there's no drain nearby. All are ENERGY STAR certified with handy Smart Dry controls. Given the thin independent reliability data and the parts-only warranty, though, we'd compare them with GE, Midea and Frigidaire before deciding on brand recognition alone.

faqs.q: What is the best Haier dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For a bedroom or office, the Haier 20-Pint (QDHR20LZ). For a damper room of similar size, the 35-Pint (QDHR35LZ). For a basement up to about 1,500 sq ft, the 50-Pint (QDHR50LZ), or the pump-equipped QPHR50LZ if there's no floor drain nearby.

Haier owns GE Appliances, but GE's current dehumidifiers are built under license by Midea, according to ENERGY STAR records. Haier's own Smart Dry models share branding and very similar specs with GE's, so they're close siblings, but they aren't documented as the same hardware.

faqs.q: Has a Haier dehumidifier been recalled?
faqs.a: Yes. The 2021 New Widetech recall included Haier models HEN70ETFP, HEN70ETFP-E, HM50EP and HM70EP made before September 1, 2017. The current QDHR and QPHR lineup isn't affected, but check any used unit's model number and date against CPSC.gov.

faqs.q: Where can I find a Haier dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Haier publishes owner's and installation manuals on its appliance support website. Search using the complete model number from the rating label on the unit. The manual covers setup, the filter, drain hose connection and error codes.

faqs.q: How do I clean the filter on a Haier dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Unplug the unit, slide out the mesh filter, rinse it in warm water (a little mild detergent is fine), let it air-dry completely and reinstall it. Then reset the clean-filter reminder. Haier's reminder typically prompts this every few weeks of running.

faqs.q: Does the Haier 50-pint dehumidifier have a pump?
faqs.a: The standard QDHR50LZ doesn't; it uses a 15-pint tank or a gravity hose. The QPHR50LZ has the same 50-pint capacity and adds a built-in pump that lifts water up to 16 feet.

faqs.q: Can a Haier portable air conditioner replace a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Not really. A portable AC's dry mode removes some moisture while cooling, but it's built to lower temperature, and it typically vents warm air outdoors. In a cool, damp basement, a dedicated dehumidifier works far better. Our [dehumidifier vs. air conditioner](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-air-conditioner/) guide explains the difference.
